3. impl KernelFrame {
4.     /// Well-formedness of a kernel-frame handle: its owned physical address is page aligned.
5.     ///
6.     /// Purely structural — it makes **no** ownership claim (it does not assert that the frame

8.     /// `into_page_address` and the `KernelStack` index arithmetic behind it assume the returned
9.     /// `FrameAddress` is page aligned. Stated entirely on the abstract address `self@`, so it
10.     /// leaks no implementation detail. Mirror of `UserFrame::inv`.
11.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {

4. //! Kernel frame type.
5. //!
6. //! A [`KernelFrame`] represents a single page-sized physical frame allocated for kernel use.
7. //! It provides `Deref`/`DerefMut` for direct kernel access (identity-mapped) and frees the
8. //! underlying frame on drop via the global frame allocator.
9. 
10. //==================================================================================================
11. // Imports
12. //==================================================================================================
13. 
14. use vstd::prelude::*;
15. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
16. include!("kframe.spec.rs");

21.     Address,
22.     FrameAddress,
23.     PageAligned,
24.     PhysicalAddress,
25. };

27. use ::core::ops::{

33. //==================================================================================================
34. // Kernel Frame
35. //==================================================================================================
36. 
37. /// A type that represents a kernel frame.
38. #[derive(Debug)]
39. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
40. pub struct KernelFrame {
41.     /// Frame address.
42.     base: FrameAddress,
43. }
44. 
45. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]

48. /// Abstract view of a kernel frame: the physical address of the owned frame.
49. impl View for KernelFrame {
50.     type V = int;
51. 
52.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
53.         self.base@
54.     }
55. }
56. 
57. } // verus!

59. // Dependency contract for the manager layer: wrapping a `FrameAddress` produces a handle whose
60. // abstract address is the same physical frame.
61. #[verus_verify]
62. impl KernelFrame {
63.     ///
64.     /// # Description
65.     ///
66.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
67.     ///
68.     /// # Parameters
69.     ///
70.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
71.     ///
72.     /// # Returns
73.     ///
74.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
75.     ///
76.     // Dependency contract: wrapping a frame goes through `mm::virt::identity_map_page`, which
77.     // is outside the verification scope of `mm::phys`. On success the returned handle owns the
78.     // same physical frame that was passed in. `external_body` per `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`:
79.     // the identity-mapping side effect lives in `mm::virt` and the body's `?`/log closures call
80.     // into that layer, so the wrap contract is trusted until `mm::virt` is verified.
81.     #[verus_spec(result =>
82.         requires
83.             base.inv(),
84.         ensures
85.             match result {
86.                 Ok(kf) => {
87.                     &&& kf@ == base@
88.                     &&& kf.inv()
89.                 },
90.                 Err(_) => true,
91.             },
92.     )]
93.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
94.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
95.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
96.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
97.         // allocation occurs).
98.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
99.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
100.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
101.                 e
102.             })?;
103.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
104.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
105.             e
106.         })?;
107.

109.     }
110. }

114. 
115.     ///
116.     /// # Description
117.     ///
118.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
119.     ///
120.     /// # Returns
121.     ///
122.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
123.     ///
124.     // Pure accessor: returns the owned frame's physical address unchanged. `result@ == self@`

127.     #[verus_spec(result =>

132.             result.inv(),

137. }

142.     /// # Description
143.     ///
144.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
145.     ///
146.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
147.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
148.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
149.     ///
150.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
151.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
152.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
153.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
154.             e
155.         })
156.     }
157. }

162. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
163. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
164. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
165. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
166. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
167.     type Target = [u8];
168. 
169.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
170.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
171.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
172.     }
173. }
174. 
175. /// # Safety
176. ///
177. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
178. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
179.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
180.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
